items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the criminal procedure law, in relation to enacting the "plea agreement immigration consequences disclosure act"
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S134

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the criminal procedure law, in
relation to enacting the "plea agreement immigration consequences
disclosure act"

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

Requires that an alien who is a defendant in the criminal justice
system be warned that the acceptance of a guilty plea may be grounds
for deportation, exclusion from admission to the United States, or
denial of naturalization.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1. Legislative Findings and Declaration

Section 2. Amends the Criminal Procedure Law, Section 170.10
subdivision 4 by adding two new paragraphs (f) and (g). Provides that
before a guilty plea is accepted by an alien, the court shall inform
the defendant that acceptance of a guilty plea or conviction may
result in such defendant's deportation, exclusion from admission to
the United States, or denial of naturalization. Provides that upon
request, the court shall allow the defendant additional time to
consider the appropriateness of the plea in light of the advisement.

Section 3. Amends the Criminal Procedure Law, Section 180.10 by adding
a new subdivision 7. Provides that before a guilty plea is accepted by
an alien, the court shall inform the defendant that acceptance of a
guilty plea or conviction may result in such defendant's deportation,
exclusion from admission to the United States, or denial of
naturalization. Provides that upon request, the court shall allow the
defendant additional time to consider the appropriateness of the plea
in light of the advisement.

Section 4. Amends the Criminal Procedure Law, Section 210.15 by adding
a new subdivision 4. Provides that if the Court fails to so advise the
defendant, such defendant will have the right to withdraw the guilty
plea. Absent an official record in the court file that the court
provided the advisement as prescribed, the defendant shall be presumed
not to have received the advisement. Allows the court to set aside the
judgment and permit the defendant to withdraw the plea.  Provides that
the defendant shall not be required at anytime during the proceedings
or at the time of the plea to disclose his or her legal status.

Section 5. Effective Date

 EXISTING LAW :

None.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Many individuals who are not citizens and are accused of a crime under
State law are not aware of the fact that acceptance of a guilty plea
could constitute grounds for deportation, exclusion from admission to
the United States, or denial of naturalization. Allowing any such
guilty plea taken in ignorance of major consequences constitutes a
denial of elementary concepts of fairness and may also constitute a
denial of due process.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2013: S.860 - Referred to Codes/A.5279 - Referred to Codes

2009-10: S.3154B - Amend and Recommit to Codes/A.5883B - Amend and
Recommit to Rules
2007-08: S.776 - Referred to Codes/ A.5191 - Held for Consideration in
Codes
2005-06: S.829 - Referred to Codes/A.4100 - Referred to Codes
2003-04; S 2836 - Motion to Petition Lost/A.5267 - Referred to Codes

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the hundredth and eightieth day after it
shall have become a law.

summary: Enacts the "plea agreement immigration consequences disclosure act"; requires a court to advise a defendant that if he or she is an alien and he or she is convicted of a crime, whether by plea or trial, such conviction may result in his or her deportation; allows a withdrawal of a plea of guilty by an alien if such alien is threatened with deportation and such alien is not so advised of such threat of deportation.
title: Enacts the "plea agreement immigration consequences disclosure act"
